name: The Journey East
description: A scrap of Japan found before the plane left. Stories travel ahead of people.

name: Edo
description: The old name of Tokyo. Edo was the Tokugawa shogunate’s political centre, then renamed Tokyo in the Meiji transition.

name: Konbini
description: A tiny kitchen that never sleeps. Onigiri, egg sandwiches and hot snacks at odd hours are a system, not a compromise.

name: Kaiju
description: A giant screen-monster. Godzilla’s head watches Kabukicho from the Shinjuku Toho Building.

name: Old Tokyo, New Tokyo
description: From Skytree you can point toward Asakusa and see the low city still sitting under the new one.

name: Hachiko
description: The Akita who kept returning to Shibuya Station for years after his owner died. The statue still waits.

name: Meiji Forest
description: The woods at Meiji Jingu were planted on purpose, designed to become a forest that could keep itself.

name: Five Creatures
description: The outer market still sells the sea. Naming every creature is optional. Noticing them is the page.

name: Constructed Land
description: Tsukiji roughly means constructed land. After the Meireki fire of 1657, this ground was packed into Tokyo Bay.

name: Sushi
description: Seasoned rice, not a synonym for raw fish. Sashimi is the slice without that rice.

name: Sampuru
description: Plastic food in a restaurant window. It shows the dish without spoiling in the sun.

name: Shinkansen Nose
description: A long nose that moves air aside, so a fast train does not punch a tunnel as hard.

name: Sumo
description: Commonly described as Japan’s national sport. The ring still carries Shinto ritual, including salt. That is not the same as most-watched.
